title: [bug][multi-device][PWA] Service Worker кеширует удалённые книги до принудительной выгрузки PWA
description: ПРОБЛЕМА: multi-device sync. На устройстве А удалил книгу (или изменил метаданные/обложку) — на устройстве Б карточка продолжает висеть в IDB cached_books даже после reload (перезагрузка IDB не чистит). Сильнее — если каталог на Б открыт одновременно с delete на А, Б вообще ничего не узнаёт до reload/focus. Требует принудительной выгрузки PWA через clear-site-data для wipe IDB. ДИАГНОЗ: SW (public/sw.js) API не кэширует (line 27: bypass /api/*). Проблема в IDB-слое (cached_books из offline-storage.ts), который клиент мёрджит с API response и никогда не invalidate'ит для orphan'ов. ФИКС (минимальный, клиентский, без backend изменений): (1) Catalog reconciliation: при успешном GET /api/books на загрузке страницы /books — intersection списка id с cached_books IDB, удаление orphan'ов через removeBookFromLocalStorage. (2) Self-healing 404: при GET /api/books/:id 404 — автоматически removeBookFromLocalStorage(id) из api/client.ts. (3) Refetch on focus + interval: visibility/focus event + setInterval(60s) refetch /api/books пока страница активна. Если проект использует React Query — refetchOnWindowFocus:true + refetchInterval:60000. Покрывает кейс 'обе вкладки открыты одновременно'. Все три — clean frontend, ~1-2 часа. Для real-time sync (мгновенное удаление, progress sync, etc) — см. отдельный bd на SSE. Trigger: Alexey увидел 'Слова сияния' + 'Проект Аве Мария' удалённые на другом устройстве, но висящие в UI локально.

ERROR PUT /api/reader/progress/927: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed

title: SQL composition rewrite: f-string → aiosql
description:
## Мотивация

Текущий паттерн DAL-слоя — shared SQL-константы (`BOOK_LIST_JOINS`, `BOOK_LIST_AGGREGATE_COLUMNS`, `_BOOK_SELECT`), интерполируемые в итоговый SQL-запрос через Python f-string. Паттерн введён в E5.2 (коммит 2c43af3), не был замечен в hl8.1, hl8.3 (L1-L5), a4l — проехал через 4 рефактор-эпика.

Проблемы:
- Итоговый SQL не видно в одном месте — нужно склеивать из двух файлов.
- Git diff'ы на SQL-изменениях нечитаемы.
- IDE не подсвечивает как SQL.
- Плохо debug'ается.
- Переписывание SELECT'ов (как требует rpus) множится по всем callsite'ам через f-string-магию.

Паттерн не является mainstream Python-практикой. Ближе к антипаттерну (хотя не injection-vulnerable в этом конкретном коде — интерполируются только собственные константы, не пользовательский ввод).

## Scope

14 мест интерполяции SQL-констант в 5 файлах DAL:
- `backend/app/dal/book_list_query.py` — удаляется целиком (константы перестают существовать).
- `backend/app/dal/books.py` — `_BOOK_SELECT` удаляется, 2 callsite'а переписываются.
- `backend/app/dal/authors.py` — 1 callsite.
- `backend/app/dal/series.py` — 1 callsite.
- `backend/app/dal/tags.py` — 1 callsite.
- `backend/app/dal/shelves.py` — 3 callsite'а (best/reading_now/regular).

Плюс dynamic f-string в `dal/books.py:56` (`ub_join = f\"AND ub.user_id = :uid\" if uid else \"AND 0\"`) — тоже сносится.

## Approach

aiosql (https://nackjicholson.github.io/aiosql/) — SQL-запросы живут в отдельных .sql-файлах, Python-код вызывает их как функции. SQL нормально diff'ается, IDE подсвечивает, никаких интерполяций Python-строк. Лёгкая зависимость (PyPI aiosql).

Альтернативы рассмотрены: SQLAlchemy Core (тяжёлая зависимость, меняет DAL-слой радикально), полное дублирование SQL per DAL-функция (лениво, масштабируется плохо). aiosql — золотая середина.

## Out of scope

- DAL API surface (сигнатуры `get_books`, `get_author_by_id` и т.д.) — не меняется.
- TypedDict row-shapes — не меняются.
- Wire contract — не меняется (этим занимается rpus).
- Business-логика DAL-функций — не меняется, только способ хранения и подстановки SQL.

## Блокирует

`librarium-py-rpus` и все его child-beды — rpus должна запускаться после того, как f-string composition снесён. Иначе rpus будет править f-string магию сразу в нескольких местах, что множит работу.

## Acceptance

- Ни одного import'а из `book_list_query.py` (файл удалён или пустой).
- Ни одной f-string-интерполяции SQL-константы или динамического SQL-фрагмента в `backend/app/dal/*.py`.
- Все DAL-функции принимают параметры через bind (`:uid`, `:id` и т.д.), без Python-склейки.
- Backend pytest зелёный.
- Wire-контракт не изменился (frontend сборка и vitest — без правок).
notes: Task 15 acceptance sweep: все grep'ы пройдены, 752 pytest passed, 102 naming tests passed. Готово к manual smoke + PR в main по команде Alexey.

title: Merrilin-style sync: version CAS + intent-aware conflict resolution + mount gate
description:
## Context

Current reading_progress sync has two open issues from code review of fix/pwa-reader-restore-flag (commits 5992def + 6159977):

- **C1 from review:** cross-device stale overwrite. Phone reads offline, laptop advances, phone comes online and its mount sync pushes stale local over laptop's fresh server state. Current synced-flag-only reconciliation has no way to detect this.
- **Timestamp drift:** we explicitly rejected wall-clock comparisons because client/server clocks diverge a few seconds.

Researched prior art — Merrilin by Stonecharioteer (article "What Was I Reading Last? In Three Not-So-Easy Pieces", March 2026) solves the exact same problem in their Account-Cloud lane. Reference: https://tech.stonecharioteer.com/posts/2026/merrilin-local-sync/

## Algorithm (from Merrilin's cloud lane)

**1. Server-owned version counter.** `reading_progress` gets `version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. Server increments on every accepted write.

**2. Compare-and-swap PUT.** Client sends `expected_version` = the version it last saw from server. Server:
  - If `current.version == expected_version` → accept, increment, return new version.
  - If `current.version != expected_version` → conflict, intent check:
    - `new.fraction >= current.fraction` → forward advance → **auto-rebase** (accept anyway, increment, mark `rebased: true`)
    - `new.fraction < current.fraction` → rewind in conflict → **reject** immediately ("another device advanced past you, your rewind is stale"), return current state so client can adopt.
  - Server-side CAS loop up to 3 retries for internal concurrency races.

**3. Mount gate.** On reader mount, cloud-bound syncs are held back until the initial server pull completes and merges with local. Prevents the C1 window where stale local overwrites fresh server between mount and first GET.

## Scope

### Backend
- `backend/schema.sql`: `ALTER TABLE reading_progress ADD COLUMN version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;`
- `backend/app/dal/reader.py`: rewrite `save_reading_progress` with CAS loop + intent check, return `{accepted, version, rebased}` or `{accepted: False, current: {...}}`
- `backend/app/routers/reader.py`: `ReadingProgressBody.expected_version: int = 0`, response passes through DAL result
- `backend/tests/test_reader.py`: TDD for all five scenarios (fresh write, clean CAS match, forward rebase, rewind reject, rejected returns current)
- Prod DB migration: run ALTER manually on server (SQLite, simple ADD COLUMN, no data migration needed)

### Frontend
- `frontend/src/utils/offline-storage.ts`: `LocalProgress` gains `serverVersion: number`. `saveProgress` preserves `serverVersion` field.
- `frontend/src/hooks/useReaderStorage.ts`:
  - `pushProgressToServer` sends `expected_version`, handles `accepted: true` (update local serverVersion from response) and `accepted: false` (adopt current from response body)
  - Mount flow: add `gateRef` — while true, `handleRelocate` writes to IDB but does NOT schedule server push. `syncProgressAndSettings` sets gate true, does initial GET + merge, sets gate false, then flushes any queued writes.
  - Reconcile logic uses version comparison, not timestamps, not synced-flag-only
  - `adoptServerProgress` updates `serverVersion` from server response

### Not in scope
- Annotations, reading events (we don't have them yet)
- Peer-to-peer lane (Merrilin's HLC-based guest-peer lane) — we're cloud-only
- File-hash-based book matching — we have internal book_id

## Scenarios to verify in tests / manual

1. **C1: phone offline unsynced + laptop advanced online**
   - Phone ends at laptop's latest after mount sync (rewind-in-conflict rejected)

2. **Forward-forward both offline**
   - First to come online: clean CAS accept
   - Second to come online: forward conflict → rebase accept → furthest-read wins

3. **Re-read online single device**
   - Clean CAS match, fraction goes down, accepted

4. **Re-read offline, laptop untouched**
   - Clean CAS match (expected == current), accepted

5. **Re-read offline, laptop advanced meanwhile**
   - Rewind in conflict → rejected → phone adopts laptop state (re-read lost, can redo manually)

6. **Mount gate: handleRelocate during gate window**
   - Writes accumulate in IDB only; pushed after gate releases

## Follow-up

After implementing: another code review pass (superpowers:code-reviewer) to catch details missed on the first read of Merrilin's article.

## References

- Merrilin sync article (source PDF saved locally at ~/Downloads/): https://tech.stonecharioteer.com/posts/2026/merrilin-local-sync/
- Plan file with detailed trace: /Users/alexey/.claude/plans/foamy-cuddling-deer.md
- Parent code review: findings C1, M1-M11, m1-m17 on branch fix/pwa-reader-restore-flag (commits 5992def, 6159977)
notes:
Additional items from code review of the PWA reader restore branch (commits 5992def + 6159977 + a8d994a) to address in this rewrite — no point fixing in the old mechanism that's being replaced:

**M1 — stalled fetch blocks the serialization chain.**
Current inFlightPutRef chain has no abort timeout. If one PUT hangs (flaky cellular, server stall), all queued PUTs wait forever. In the new implementation add AbortController with ~10s timeout for non-keepalive pushes. Keepalive pushes (flushProgress on pagehide/visibilitychange/unmount) should stay untimed.

**M2 — pushProgressToServer order-of-ops: markProgressSynced failure swallows success.**
Current order: resp.ok → await markProgressSynced → ok=true. If markProgressSynced throws (Safari storage pressure), ok stays false, caller thinks failure, local stays synced=false, next sync re-pushes uselessly. In the new impl: set ok=true BEFORE the IDB write, wrap markProgressSynced in try/catch. Server is the source of truth.

**M3 — eventually-consistent markProgressSynced.**
flush1 writes P1 synced=false, queues PUT1. flush2 writes P2 synced=false (overwrites), queues PUT2. PUT1 completes, markProgressSynced marks the row (now P2) as synced=true — but server still has P1 until PUT2 lands. Brief invariant violation. Practical impact: zero, PUT2 lands right after and everything converges. With version counter replacing the synced flag, this goes away — version mismatch is the precise signal.

**M4 — getLastReadBook unfiltered scan.**
No filter for rows with missing lastReadAt or lastFormat. Old pre-field rows (if any) could cause the reduce to return garbage. Add filter: `all.filter(p => p.lastReadAt && p.lastFormat)` before the max reduce.

**M5 — restore effect runs without waiting for auth.**
App.tsx restore effect fires navigate(savedURL) immediately at mount, before /api/auth/me resolves. URL updates while ProtectedRoute shows "Загрузка...". Works in happy path. Corner case: auth check fails → ProtectedRoute → /login → LoginPage clears flag. Document this; consider waiting for auth.loading===false before the async GET+navigate.

**M6 — mid-session 401 not handled.**
Already tracked as librarium-py-46g. Pre-existing.

**M7 — unmount-time flush survives via keepalive, but depends on prior non-keepalive PUTs not blocking the chain.**
Addressed transitively by M1 fix (timeout) and by new outbox-style design.

**M8 — flushProgress cleanup effect re-runs on identity change.**
Not a bug today. Skip unless the new impl reintroduces the concern.

**M11 — handleRelocate double-saves (immediate + debounced flush).**
Pre-existing. New outbox-based impl should have a single write path (IDB immediate, server debounced through outbox queue) so this goes away.

**Minor items (m1-m17 from review, mostly nits):**
- m6: Refresh-in-reader → history stack = [reader] → Close button is a no-op. Pre-existing. Consider fallback navigate("/") when history.length <= 1 in exitReader.
- m7: useReaderLifecycle reload on detached view interacts fine with flag restore (isReading guard catches re-entry).
- m8: **No tests.** Project is TDD-first. New impl MUST have tests: getLastReadBook variants, markProgressSynced preserves lastReadAt, CAS version semantics (accept/rebase/reject), mount-gate behavior.
- m10: adoptServerProgress writes server last_read_at into local lastReadAt — muddy semantics with getLastReadBook relying on lastReadAt for "which book to restore". Document or split into two fields.
- m12: lastFormat casing — normalize at write time, not at read time.
- m14/m15: onClick type should probably be (e: React.MouseEvent) => void if we add modifier-key guards later (Mi2 — deferred per user).
- C2 (from review): resume() mixes ref-based and direct-closure callback patterns. In the new impl, stick to one pattern (prefer refs).

**Testing requirements for the new implementation:**
- Backend tests for CAS: fresh write, clean match, forward rebase, rewind reject, rejected response body shape
- Frontend tests for the mount gate mechanism
- Frontend tests for getLastReadBook (empty, multi-row, missing fields)
- Frontend tests for pushProgressToServer: accept, rebase, reject-and-adopt
- Manual scenario tests (see "Scenarios to verify" in main description)
close_reason:
Shipped on main (merge b3ea3bb).

Implementation:
- backend/schema.sql: version column in reading_progress CREATE TABLE
- backend/app/dal/reader.py: CAS with AND version = :expected on both UPDATEs, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on INSERT, rowcount guards + retry x3, intent-aware forward-rebase / rewind-reject
- backend/app/routers/reader.py: ReadingProgressBody.expected_version, DAL result returned transparently
- frontend/src/utils/reader-sync.ts (new): shared pushProgressToServerCAS helper used by both useReaderStorage and main.tsx's syncUnsyncedProgress
- frontend/src/utils/offline-storage.ts: LocalProgress.serverVersion, atomic saveProgress/markProgressSynced, adoptServerProgressLocal helper, getLastReadBook, DB_VERSION bump 2→3
- frontend/src/hooks/useReaderStorage.ts: pushProgressToServer via CAS helper + FIFO chain + 10s abort timeout, resumeGateRef guards handleRelocate during resume(), flushProgress read-back for fresh serverVersion
- frontend/src/main.tsx: syncUnsyncedProgress via shared CAS helper
- frontend/src/pages/desktop/DesktopPdfReaderPage.tsx: resumePosition subscription for mid-session adopt

Two rounds of code review, all findings addressed. Prod DB migrated manually (ALTER + backfill v=1 on 16 rows), backup at db.sqlite.bak-20260410-175452. Manually tested on tablet+desktop, PDF sync confirmed working.

Tests: 341/341 backend, 46/46 frontend, build clean.

title: PWA: исследовать и починить lifecycle при уходе/возврате из фона
description: Проблемы: 1) позиция чтения не передаётся при блокировке экрана (beforeunload не срабатывает на iOS Safari PWA). 2) Читалка не восстанавливается при возврате из фона. 3) Позиция передаётся через раз. Нужно: исследовать visibilitychange / pagehide / freeze events на iOS Safari PWA, понять что работает, починить flush прогресса + восстановление читалки.
notes:
PWA Reader Lifecycle plan:

Principle
- IndexedDB is the only hard guarantee. Network flush on hidden/pagehide is best effort with keepalive.
- One arbiter for reader progress while the reader is open: useReaderStorage.
- On resume, compare server position with the freshest local position, not just timestamps.

Plan
1. useReaderStorage.ts
- Save reading progress to IndexedDB on every relocate without debounce.
- Reduce server debounce from 3s to 1s.
- Add keepalive: true to progress PUT in flushProgress.
- Flush on visibilitychange(hidden) and pagehide.
- Track two refs: lastPositionRef for freshest in-memory position and lastSavedPositionRef for last flushed JSON position.
- On visibilitychange(visible), if online, GET /api/reader/progress/{id}; compare against freshest local position (lastPositionRef if present, otherwise lastSavedPositionRef). If different, expose resumePosition for ReaderPage to apply via goTo().
- Unify initial syncProgressAndSettings with the same arbitration model: if local progress is unsynced, push local; if synced and server position differs, apply server. Avoid timestamp-only decisions.
- Expose resumePosition and clearResumePosition from the hook.

2. offline-storage.ts
- Update markProgressSynced to set synced=true and refresh lastReadAt for compatibility with any remaining timestamp-based reads.

3. DesktopReaderPage.tsx / MobileReaderPage.tsx
- Watch resumePosition and call view.goTo(resumePosition), then clear it.
- On visibilitychange(visible), if foliate-view/renderer is gone, reload the page to reconstruct from cache/network through useReaderStorage.
- Manage a reader-active flag with mount/unmount symmetry so global sync can stand down while the reader is open.

4. main.tsx
- Keep global unsynced push for non-reader app states only.
- Skip global reading_progress sync while a reader is active; settings sync may stay global.
- Add visibilitychange(visible) push path with the same reader-active guard.

Verification
- Cold-start cross-device sync: finish reading on device A, then open the PWA reader for the same book on device B; B must open at A's latest server position on first load.
- Resume cross-device sync: keep the same book open on A and B; read on A, background A, return to B; B should jump only when server position truly differs.
- Same-device resume without remote changes: background and return to the same reader; no false jump.
- Lock/sleep on device A, then open on device B: latest position should arrive.
- Let iOS kill the PWA reader process; resume should reload and restore from cache/network with correct progress.
- Run frontend tests after implementation.

title: Ридер: обложка как нулевая страница, исключённая из счётчика прогресса
description:
Открывающая позиция FB2/EPUB-книги: обложка моделируется как нулевая страница в обычной модели книги/секций, а первый текстовый section остаётся первой читаемой страницей. Реализация не должна быть overlay поверх ридера и не должна вводить отдельный слой перехвата событий.

Зависит от b4ci.1: обложка должна прилегать к уже скомпонованному фронтматеру, а не пересобирать фронтматер сама.

Что сделать:
1) Для EPUB использовать native cover spine page, если она уже есть в reading order; пометить её как cover/non-counted и сделать навигируемой.
2) Для FB2 добавить нулевую cover section из metadata coverpage, потому что реальные FB2 в data/library держат обложку в description/title-info/coverpage, а не в body.
3) Если у книги нет доступной картинки обложки, создать спокойный fallback cover section с названием/автором.
4) Навигация: Prev с первой текстовой страницы ведёт на обложку; Next с обложки ведёт на первую текстовую страницу; явный переход в начало книги открывает обложку.
5) TOC: добавить первый пункт «Обложка» с href="__cover__". Остальные TOC entries должны вести в те же текстовые места семантически и не ломаться от сдвига section indexes.
6) Footer/progress: на обложке показывать «Обложка»; текстовый счётчик начинается с 1 / N. Total N, fraction и виртуальные страницы считаются только по counted text sections.
7) Сохранение прогресса: нахождение на обложке не записывается как reading-progress. Старые saved text CFI/fake-CFI должны открывать те же текстовые места.
8) Старт без saved text position открывает cover через обычный view.goTo(0), потому что поддерживаемые FB2/EPUB книги нормализуются так, что book.sections[0] — cover. Legacy-ветвление ради MOBI/CBZ в этой задаче не нужно.

Тесты:
- unit/integration: progress excludes counted=false; FB2 old fake-CFI compatibility; FB2 TOC/frontmatter semantic preservation; EPUB native cover, synthetic cover, no-cover fallback; EPUB CFI offset only for synthetic cover; no-save cover through pagehide and explicit TOC navigation; footer cover label and unchanged N;
- manual: FB2/EPUB books from data/library with existing saved progress, Prev/Next, TOC, footer, first text page 1 / N, native EPUB cover not duplicated.
design:
Обложка является полноценной нулевой позицией книги в едином reader navigation flow.

Решение:
- Не использовать overlay и не заводить отдельный слой перехвата tap/click/keyboard событий.
- Представить обложку как cover section внутри book/section model: native для EPUB, synthetic для FB2 metadata-only, fallback для книг без картинки.
- Cover section имеет isCover=true, counted=false, size=0, charCount=0 и не участвует в расчёте размера, fraction и виртуальных страниц.
- В footer на обложке показывается «Обложка»; первая текстовая страница показывает 1 / N.
- Обложка доступна всегда: Prev с первой текстовой страницы ведёт на неё, Next с неё ведёт в текст, TOC содержит первый пункт «Обложка».
- Сохранённая текстовая позиция имеет приоритет над автоматическим показом обложки. Переход на обложку через TOC не затирает saved text progress.
- Старые FB2 fake-CFI и EPUB CFI должны резолвиться в те же текстовые места; любые внутренние offsets применяются только на resolver boundary.
- Native EPUB cover с linear="no" должен быть нормализован как навигируемая cover position, иначе Prev с первой текстовой страницы может пропустить обложку.
- Runtime старт без saved position остаётся простым: view.goTo(0). Сложность должна быть в нормализации FB2/EPUB book model, а не в legacy-ветвлении форматов.

Причина: EPUB/FB2 обложка концептуально вшита в книгу, поэтому она должна быть достижимой как обычная начальная позиция. При этом прогресс и размер книги должны описывать только читаемый текст.

title: FB2: визуальный разделитель *** между склеенными блоками
description:
После склейки нескольких смысловых блоков в один render-section (см. b4ci.1) нужен видимый визуальный разделитель, чтобы блоки не сливались — три центрированные звёздочки * * * (асвдискус/орнамент). Где появляется: - между сводным титулом и блоком копирайтов на правой странице открывающего разворота - между шапкой части (title+карта) и началом первой главы - перед/после одинокого эпиграфа, склеенного с соседним содержательным куском Реализация: - в FB2Converter (fb2.js) при склейке вставлять элемент-разделитель между блоками:
* * *
или аналогичный - стилизовать в inlined CSS (style blob, fb2.js:207): центрирование, vertical margin ~2em, font-size как у текста, опциональный приглушённый цвет - учитывать, что page-break поведение paginator-а: разделитель не должен оставаться орфаном внизу страницы (page-break-after: avoid? или break-inside: avoid на склееном куске?) Карта части (большая иллюстрация) хочет естественного column-break после себя, чтобы текст начинался со следующей страницы — проверить, нужен ли явный CSS на image, или paginator сам справится при достаточном размере картинки. По решению пользователя — не делаем магию: разделитель *** между картой и текстом, paginator решит. Тесты: визуальная регрессия — 5-10 разнотипных книг (Корсаков/930, Розенберг/802 если применимо, Сандерсон/920, обычная классика) — скриншоты до/после, ручная проверка что (а) разделитель виден, (б) блоки не слипаются, (в) разделитель не висит сиротой.
notes: Уточнение к описанию (потерялось при создании из-за шелл-эскейпинга): про карту части — проверить, нужен ли явный CSS свойство break-after со значением column на image, или paginator сам справится при достаточном размере картинки.
close_reason: Не понадобились — после b4ci.1 (frontmatter wrapper в отдельную render-section) визуально проверка Alexey'я подтвердила что естественной CSS-стилизации wrapper-классов (.title, .epigraph, .cite) достаточно, явные *** разделители не нужны.

title: FB2: склейка худых секций фронтматера и шапок частей в один render-section
description: Расширить логику mergeHeadingIntros в frontend/src/vendor/foliate-js/fb2.js (строки 446-473), чтобы склеивать со следующим содержательным куском не только heading-only секции ≤500 chars, но также: 1) Декоративный фронтматер на верхнем уровне body: подряд идущие и <section> без прозовых <p> корневого уровня (или <500 chars прозы) — копирайты, посвящения. Граница — первая «прозаическая» секция (≥3 прозовых <p> на корневом уровне ИЛИ ≥1500 chars прозы). 2) Шапка части — section, у которой первый сегмент после splitSection это только <title>+<image>+<epigraph> без прозы, но дальше идут вложенные <section> с главами. Первый сегмент должен приклеиваться к началу следующего сегмента (первой главе). 3) Одинокий эпиграф книги/главы — section, состоящая из одного <epigraph> или <poem> без прозы, независимо от char count. Не трогать: - содержательные секции (предисловия, благодарности, «От автора», глоссарии) — это полноценные главы по эвристике ≥3 prose-p или ≥1500 chars prose - body[name='notes'] (сноски) — отдельный body, остаётся как есть - структуру TOC и href-резолверы Нужно отделять склеенные блоки внутри одного render-section'а — это отдельная задача (Visual divider * * *), эта задача только про склейку. Тесты: расширить frontend/src/vendor/foliate-js/fb2.test.ts. Регрессионный sweep на 54 FB2-файла из data/library — диффать количество render-sections и виды первых 5 секций до/после. Статистика для контекста — 54 книги: - 67% имеют ≥2 секций фронтматера, median длина 187 chars, 81% укладываются в 500 chars - топ-паттерны: 14× title→copyright, 13× только title, 4× title→copyright→copyright - edge case 1 (книга 802, Розенберг): praise+preface+acknowledgments — НЕ склеиваем, защищает порог prose - edge case 2 (книга 930, Корсаков): Часть I+карта, должна приклеиваться к главе I
close_reason: Merged into main via merge commit. FB2 frontmatter compaction shipped. Manual verification done by Alexey on 5 books (Эриксон, Корсаков ×2, Сandersон, Рубина); known limitation on Rosenberg 802 (cite-wrapped praise treated as decorative) accepted.

title: Ридер: открывающий разворот + компактный фронтматер FB2
description:
Цель — убрать пустые/полупустые страницы в начале FB2-книги и придать ридеру нормальный книжный открывающий разворот. По статистике на 54 файлах: 67% книг имеют ≥2 секций декоративного фронтматера до текста (титул+копирайт+посвящение), и многие имеют отдельные «пустые» страницы под шапку части (title+карта/иллюстрация) и под одинокий эпиграф. Это даёт 3-6 переворотов перед первой строчкой. Решения по UX: - открывающий разворот: слева обложка, справа сводный титул-блок (автор+название+копирайт) - обложка НЕ входит в счётчик прогресса - внутри склеенных блоков визуальный разделитель — три центрированные звёздочки * * * - шапка части (title+карта) и одинокий эпиграф — приклеиваются к ближайшему содержательному куску через тот же разделитель - декоративный фронтматер склеиваем; содержательный (предисловие, благодарности, «От автора» в нон-фикшене) НЕ трогаем — порог: ≥3 прозовых

корневого уровня или ≥1500 chars прозы Эпик распадается на 3 подзадачи (см. зависимости).

# eqt.2 — `useEbookReaderInstance()` extraction from `ebook-reader.tsx`

**Issue:** librarium-py-eqt.2
**Parent epic:** librarium-py-eqt (F4. Reader subsystem boundary cleanup)
**Date:** 2026-05-05
**Branch:** `refactor/eqt.2-use-ebook-reader-instance` (already created)

## Goal

Distill the ~108-line `bookBlob`-scoped `useEffect` from `ebook-reader.tsx` (lines 91–198 in current state on `main`) into a dedicated hook `useEbookReaderInstance()`. **Behavior preserved bit-for-bit.** Pure code reorganization.

## Motivation

The `[bookBlob]`-scoped `useEffect` is the single biggest cluster of imperative glue between React and foliate-js in the reader subsystem. It owns:

- creation and DOM-attachment of the `<foliate-view>` custom element
- wiring the `NavigationController`
- attachment of 5 listener categories (interaction, relocate, load, link/footnote, global resize, global pagehide)
- the `view.open(blob)` flow with initial navigation and char-count startup
- full cleanup including dispose flags

It's structurally one cohesive vertical (the live foliate instance lifecycle), but it's currently inlined in the component, mixed with the rest of `EbookReader`'s state and props. Pulling it into a dedicated hook lets the component become a thin shell composing four hooks (`useFootnoteState`, `useReaderFooter`, `useEbookReaderInstance`, `useImperativeHandle`) plus the small settings-applier `useEffect` and the JSX.

Expected post-distill size of `ebook-reader.tsx`: roughly 90–100 lines (down from current ~217), depending on hook input wiring.

## Scope

### In scope

- New file `frontend/src/hooks/useEbookReaderInstance.ts`.
- New unit tests `frontend/src/hooks/useEbookReaderInstance.test.tsx` (colocated, matching dominant pattern in `frontend/src/hooks/`).
- Refactor `frontend/src/components/ebook-reader.tsx` to consume the hook.

### Out of scope

- The settings-applier `useEffect` (lines 62–81). Stays inline. Separately decided as low-value distill.
- `useImperativeHandle` block (lines 84–88). Stays inline — it owns the public ref shape and reads `viewRef`/`performNavigationRef` directly.
- Any change to `utils/reader-navigation.ts`, `utils/reader-interaction.ts`, `utils/reader-footnote-handler.ts`, `utils/reader-input.ts`, `utils/reader-styling.ts`, `hooks/useReaderFooter.ts`, `hooks/useFootnoteState.ts`, `FootnotePopup.tsx`, foliate-js fork, or any reader-side type.
- Any UX, gesture, navigation, or persistence change.
- `pdf-reader.tsx` (separate epic subtask `qhe`).

## Hook contract

```ts
import type { MutableRefObject, RefObject } from "react";
import type { ReaderSettings } from "../types/reader-settings";
import type { ReaderViewElement } from "../types/reader-foliate";
import type { ReaderNavigationRequest } from "../types/reader-handle";
import type { FootnoteState } from "./useFootnoteState";

export interface EbookReaderInstanceConfig {
  maxInlineSize: string;
  gap: string;
  margin: string | undefined;
  maxBlockSize: string | undefined;
  showFooter: boolean;
  isMobile: boolean;
}

export interface UseEbookReaderInstanceParams {
  bookBlob: Blob;
  initialPosition: string | null | undefined;
  containerRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>;
  viewRef: MutableRefObject<ReaderViewElement | null>;
  performNavigationRef: MutableRefObject<(request: ReaderNavigationRequest) => Promise<void>>;
  callbacksRef: MutableRefObject<{
    onRelocate?: (detail: import("../types/reader-handle").ReaderRelocateDetail) => void;
    onReady?: () => void;
    onSavePosition?: (cfi: string, fraction: number) => void;
  } | undefined>;
  onCenterTapRef: MutableRefObject<(() => void) | undefined>;
  settingsRef: MutableRefObject<ReaderSettings>;
  configRef: MutableRefObject<EbookReaderInstanceConfig>;
  footnote: FootnoteState;
  footer: ReturnType<typeof import("./useReaderFooter").useReaderFooter>;
}

export function useEbookReaderInstance(params: UseEbookReaderInstanceParams): void;
```

Returns nothing. Side-effect-only hook. Internally a single `useEffect` with `[bookBlob]` deps that mirrors today's behavior exactly.

### Why a single big params object

Eleven inputs is a lot, but every one of them is required by the existing inlined effect. A flat object keeps call sites readable and avoids the temptation to reorder positional args. All 11 are stable references (refs or scalars derived from props); only `bookBlob` controls re-runs.

### Why `void` return

The hook owns the foliate-view's lifecycle but does not own ownership of `viewRef` or `performNavigationRef` — those live in the component because `useImperativeHandle` and the settings-applier effect read them. The hook writes through them. This is the cleanest split given that we explicitly leave those two pieces inlined.

## Behavior preservation

The new effect inside the hook is a verbatim move of lines 91–198 from `ebook-reader.tsx` on `main`. No rewrites, no condensation, no reordering of statements — direct relocation. The only adjustments:

- Names that previously closed over component-local refs (`viewRef`, `performNavigationRef`, `callbacksRef`, `onCenterTapRef`, `settingsRef`, `configRef`) become `params.viewRef.current = ...` and similar.
- `footnote.isOpenRef.current`, `footnote.dismiss`, `footnote.handlerCallbacks`, `footnote.lastClickXRef`, `footnote.clickYRef` become `params.footnote.…`.
- `footer.recalcPages()`, `footer.updateFooter(...)`, `footer.startCharCount(...)`, `footer.cleanupCharCount()` become `params.footer.…`.
- `bookBlob`, `initialPosition` become `params.bookBlob`, `params.initialPosition`.
- The `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` comment moves with the effect.

| Existing behavior | Preserved by |
|---|---|
| View created and removed exactly once per `bookBlob` change | Same `useEffect` deps `[params.bookBlob]`. |
| `disposed` / `disposedRef` flags guard async work after unmount | Block moved as-is. |
| `nav` controller wired with `onSavePosition`/`onReady`/`isDisposed` | Block moved as-is, including `callbacksRef` indirection. |
| All five listener attachments + their cleanups | Block moved as-is. |
| Initial navigation: `goTo(initialPosition)` if present, else `goToTextStart`/`goTo(0)` | Block moved as-is, reads `params.initialPosition`. |
| Layout attrs set on renderer at open time | Block moved as-is, reads `params.configRef.current` and `params.settingsRef.current`. |
| Char-count start after initial nav | Block moved as-is, calls `params.footer.startCharCount`. |
| Localhost-only `console.log` of open timing | Moves with the block. |
| Cleanup order: dispose flag → footer cleanup → globals → view listeners → renderer.destroy → view.close → view.remove → ref reset | Block moved as-is. |

## Test plan

### New: `useEbookReaderInstance.test.tsx`

Three pin-tests in `jsdom`. Goal: catch the structural breaks that the broader `ebook-reader.test.tsx` would also catch but pin them at the hook boundary so a future refactor of the hook in isolation is testable.

1. **Mount: foliate-view appended to container, viewRef populated, then cleaned up on unmount.** Render a wrapper that calls `useEbookReaderInstance(params)` with minimal stubs (real container div, blob, fake refs, fake `footnote`/`footer`). Assert: `container.querySelector("foliate-view")` non-null after render; viewRef.current set. After unmount: `container.children.length === 0`; viewRef.current === null.
2. **Global resize / pagehide listeners attach on mount and detach on unmount.** Spy on `globalThis.addEventListener` / `removeEventListener` for both event names. After mount: each added at least once. After unmount: each removed at least the number of times it was added. Mirrors today's `ebook-reader.test.tsx` "no leak" test, but at the hook boundary.
3. **Empty `bookBlob` short-circuits.** If `bookBlob` is falsy (or `containerRef.current` is null), no foliate-view appended. (Today's effect has an early return on these conditions.)

Use `renderHook` from `@testing-library/react` with a wrapper that provides a real `<div ref={containerRef}>` since the effect inserts into it.

### Existing tests stay green

- `frontend/src/components/ebook-reader.test.tsx` — both existing tests (smoke render + resize/pagehide leak) keep passing unchanged. They're integration tests and continue to exercise the same code through the component.
- All hook tests (`useFootnoteState`, `useReaderLifecycle`, `useReaderSettings`, `useReaderPosition`, `useReaderFooter`, etc.) — untouched.
- All `utils/reader-*.test.*` tests — untouched.

Full suite expected to remain at **727+ tests passing** (existing 727 plus 3 new pins).

## Manual smoke test (Alexey)

Per F4-stage convention, focus on FB2:

1. Open a book → text appears, navigation works (next/prev, taps, keyboard arrows, mobile zones).
2. Open a book with saved progress → resumes at the saved position.
3. Open one book → navigate to another book (different bookBlob) → first book's listeners released, new book mounts cleanly. No phantom resize/pagehide pages.
4. Footnotes still open on tap, dismiss on center-tap. (Cross-check that eqt.1 still works.)
5. Close the tab while reading → progress saved (pagehide).
6. Resize the window → footer page count recalculated.

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Cleanup-order mistake in the move | Block moved verbatim; cleanup statements stay in identical order. Test #2 pins listener cleanup. |
| `disposed` / `disposedRef` flag scoping breaks if accidentally pulled out of effect | They live as `let disposed = false` / `const disposedRef = { current: false }` inside the effect's body. Move stays inside the effect closure. Reviewer (and tests) will catch any escape. |
| Ref-write timing if the hook's effect runs in different order than original | Hook is the only effect that touches `viewRef.current` and `performNavigationRef.current`. Other effects (settings applier, `useImperativeHandle`) read them lazily via `viewRef.current` / `performNavigationRef.current(...)`. Order doesn't matter. |
| `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` survives the move | Comment included verbatim. Plan reiterates. |
| Future maintainer adds a stale-closure dep to the hook's effect | The hook explicitly takes refs (not values) for everything that varies at runtime. Dep array stays `[params.bookBlob]`. |

## Acceptance

- `frontend/src/hooks/useEbookReaderInstance.ts` exists with the contract above.
- `frontend/src/hooks/useEbookReaderInstance.test.tsx` exists with 3 pin-tests, all passing.
- `ebook-reader.tsx` shrinks: target line count ≤ 110 (down from ~217); the entire `[bookBlob]`-scoped effect body is gone from the component, replaced by one `useEbookReaderInstance({...})` call.
- All previously-green tests stay green.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Manual smoke items above all pass on Alexey's run.

Expected post-distill size of `ebook-reader.tsx`: roughly 90–100 lines (down from current ~217), depending on hook input wiring.

## Scope

### In scope

- New file `frontend/src/hooks/useEbookReaderInstance.ts`.
- New unit tests `frontend/src/hooks/useEbookReaderInstance.test.tsx` (colocated, matching dominant pattern in `frontend/src/hooks/`).
- Refactor `frontend/src/components/ebook-reader.tsx` to consume the hook.

### Out of scope

- The settings-applier `useEffect` (lines 62–81). Stays inline. Separately decided as low-value distill.
- `useImperativeHandle` block (lines 84–88). Stays inline — it owns the public ref shape and reads `viewRef`/`performNavigationRef` directly.
- Any change to `utils/reader-navigation.ts`, `utils/reader-interaction.ts`, `utils/reader-footnote-handler.ts`, `utils/reader-input.ts`, `utils/reader-styling.ts`, `hooks/useReaderFooter.ts`, `hooks/useFootnoteState.ts`, `FootnotePopup.tsx`, foliate-js fork, or any reader-side type.
- Any UX, gesture, navigation, or persistence change.
- `pdf-reader.tsx` (separate epic subtask `qhe`).

## Hook contract

```ts
import type { MutableRefObject, RefObject } from "react";
import type { ReaderSettings } from "../types/reader-settings";
import type { ReaderViewElement } from "../types/reader-foliate";
import type { ReaderNavigationRequest } from "../types/reader-handle";
import type { FootnoteState } from "./useFootnoteState";

export interface EbookReaderInstanceConfig {
  maxInlineSize: string;
  gap: string;
  margin: string | undefined;
  maxBlockSize: string | undefined;
  showFooter: boolean;
  isMobile: boolean;
}

export interface UseEbookReaderInstanceParams {
  bookBlob: Blob;
  initialPosition: string | null | undefined;
  containerRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>;
  viewRef: MutableRefObject<ReaderViewElement | null>;
  performNavigationRef: MutableRefObject<(request: ReaderNavigationRequest) => Promise<void>>;
  callbacksRef: MutableRefObject<{
    onRelocate?: (detail: import("../types/reader-handle").ReaderRelocateDetail) => void;
    onReady?: () => void;
    onSavePosition?: (cfi: string, fraction: number) => void;
  } | undefined>;
  onCenterTapRef: MutableRefObject<(() => void) | undefined>;
  settingsRef: MutableRefObject<ReaderSettings>;
  configRef: MutableRefObject<EbookReaderInstanceConfig>;
  footnote: FootnoteState;
  footer: ReturnType<typeof import("./useReaderFooter").useReaderFooter>;
}

export function useEbookReaderInstance(params: UseEbookReaderInstanceParams): void;
```

Returns nothing. Side-effect-only hook. Internally a single `useEffect` with `[bookBlob]` deps that mirrors today's behavior exactly.

### Why a single big params object

Eleven inputs is a lot, but every one of them is required by the existing inlined effect. A flat object keeps call sites readable and avoids the temptation to reorder positional args. All 11 are stable references (refs or scalars derived from props); only `bookBlob` controls re-runs.

### Why `void` return

The hook owns the foliate-view's lifecycle but does not own ownership of `viewRef` or `performNavigationRef` — those live in the component because `useImperativeHandle` and the settings-applier effect read them. The hook writes through them. This is the cleanest split given that we explicitly leave those two pieces inlined.

## Behavior preservation

The new effect inside the hook is a verbatim move of lines 91–198 from `ebook-reader.tsx` on `main`. No rewrites, no condensation, no reordering of statements — direct relocation. The only adjustments:

- Names that previously closed over component-local refs (`viewRef`, `performNavigationRef`, `callbacksRef`, `onCenterTapRef`, `settingsRef`, `configRef`) become `params.viewRef.current = ...` and similar.
- `footnote.isOpenRef.current`, `footnote.dismiss`, `footnote.handlerCallbacks`, `footnote.lastClickXRef`, `footnote.clickYRef` become `params.footnote.…`.
- `footer.recalcPages()`, `footer.updateFooter(...)`, `footer.startCharCount(...)`, `footer.cleanupCharCount()` become `params.footer.…`.
- `bookBlob`, `initialPosition` become `params.bookBlob`, `params.initialPosition`. `params.initialPosition` is captured once per `[params.bookBlob]`-run, identical to today: a change to `initialPosition` without a blob change is silently ignored, by design.
- The `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` comment moves with the effect.

| Existing behavior | Preserved by |
|---|---|
| View created and removed exactly once per `bookBlob` change | Same `useEffect` deps `[params.bookBlob]`. |
| `disposed` / `disposedRef` flags guard async work after unmount | Block moved as-is. |
| `nav` controller wired with `onSavePosition`/`onReady`/`isDisposed` | Block moved as-is, including `callbacksRef` indirection. |
| All five listener attachments + their cleanups | Block moved as-is. |
| Initial navigation: `goTo(initialPosition)` if present, else `goToTextStart`/`goTo(0)` | Block moved as-is, reads `params.initialPosition`. |
| Layout attrs set on renderer at open time | Block moved as-is, reads `params.configRef.current` and `params.settingsRef.current`. |
| Char-count start after initial nav | Block moved as-is, calls `params.footer.startCharCount`. |
| Localhost-only `console.log` of open timing | Moves with the block. |
| Cleanup order: dispose flag → footer cleanup → globals → view listeners → renderer.destroy → view.close → view.remove → ref reset | Block moved as-is. |

## Test plan

### New: `useEbookReaderInstance.test.tsx`

Three pin-tests in `jsdom`. Goal: catch the structural breaks that the broader `ebook-reader.test.tsx` would also catch but pin them at the hook boundary so a future refactor of the hook in isolation is testable.

1. **Mount: foliate-view appended to container, viewRef populated, then cleaned up on unmount.** Render a wrapper that calls `useEbookReaderInstance(params)` with minimal stubs (real container div, blob, fake refs, fake `footnote`/`footer`). Assert: `container.querySelector("foliate-view")` non-null after render; viewRef.current set. After unmount: `container.querySelector("foliate-view") === null`; viewRef.current === null. (Don't assert `children.length === 0` — at the hook test boundary the test fixture itself owns the container, so checking the foliate-view is the right level.)
2. **Global resize / pagehide listeners attach on mount and detach on unmount.** Spy on `globalThis.addEventListener` / `removeEventListener` for both event names. After mount: each added at least once. After unmount: each removed at least the number of times it was added. Mirrors today's `ebook-reader.test.tsx` "no leak" test, but at the hook boundary.
3. **Empty `bookBlob` short-circuits.** If `bookBlob` is falsy (or `containerRef.current` is null), no foliate-view appended. (Today's effect has an early return on these conditions.)

Use `renderHook` from `@testing-library/react` with a wrapper that provides a real `<div ref={containerRef}>` since the effect inserts into it.

### Existing tests stay green

- `frontend/src/components/ebook-reader.test.tsx` — both existing tests (smoke render + resize/pagehide leak) keep passing unchanged. They're integration tests and continue to exercise the same code through the component.
- All hook tests (`useFootnoteState`, `useReaderLifecycle`, `useReaderSettings`, `useReaderPosition`, `useReaderFooter`, etc.) — untouched.
- All `utils/reader-*.test.*` tests — untouched.

Full suite expected to remain at **727+ tests passing** (existing 727 plus 3 new pins).

## Manual smoke test (Alexey)

Per F4-stage convention, focus on FB2:

1. Open a book → text appears, navigation works (next/prev, taps, keyboard arrows, mobile zones).
2. Open a book with saved progress → resumes at the saved position.
3. Open one book → navigate to another book (different bookBlob) → first book's listeners released, new book mounts cleanly. No phantom resize/pagehide pages.
4. Footnotes still open on tap, dismiss on center-tap. (Cross-check that eqt.1 still works.)
5. Close the tab while reading → progress saved (pagehide).
6. Resize the window → footer page count recalculated.

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Cleanup-order mistake in the move | Block moved verbatim; cleanup statements stay in identical order. Test #2 pins listener cleanup. |
| `disposed` / `disposedRef` flag scoping breaks if accidentally pulled out of effect | They live as `let disposed = false` / `const disposedRef = { current: false }` inside the effect's body. Move stays inside the effect closure. Reviewer (and tests) will catch any escape. |
| Ref-write timing if the hook's effect runs in different order than original | Hook is the only effect that touches `viewRef.current` and `performNavigationRef.current`. Other effects (settings applier, `useImperativeHandle`) read them lazily via `viewRef.current` / `performNavigationRef.current(...)`. Order doesn't matter. |
| `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` survives the move | Comment included verbatim. Plan reiterates. |
| Future maintainer adds a stale-closure dep to the hook's effect | The hook explicitly takes refs (not values) for everything that varies at runtime. Dep array stays `[params.bookBlob]`. |
| Reflex to "harden" async race in `view.open(blob).then(...)` by adding a fresh `disposed` check between `setAttribute` calls (lines 156-160 today) | Strictly forbidden — behavior is preserved bit-for-bit. The current code only checks `disposed` at re-entry points (after `await`). The `try { view.renderer?.destroy?.(); } catch {}` at line 191 is the deliberate safety net for late-arriving renderer access. Do not add new guards during the move. |

## Acceptance

- `frontend/src/hooks/useEbookReaderInstance.ts` exists with the contract above.
- `frontend/src/hooks/useEbookReaderInstance.test.tsx` exists with 3 pin-tests, all passing.
- `ebook-reader.tsx` shrinks: target line count ≤ 130 (down from ~217); the entire `[bookBlob]`-scoped effect body is gone from the component, replaced by one `useEbookReaderInstance({...})` call. The ~108 lines removed minus ~12-15 added for the params object call site is the realistic delta; ≤ 110 was overly aggressive.
- All previously-green tests stay green.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Manual smoke items above all pass on Alexey's run.

# eqt.2 — `useEbookReaderInstance()` extraction from `ebook-reader.tsx`

**Issue:** librarium-py-eqt.2
**Parent epic:** librarium-py-eqt (F4. Reader subsystem boundary cleanup)
**Date:** 2026-05-05
**Branch:** `refactor/eqt.2-use-ebook-reader-instance` (already created)

## Goal

Distill the ~108-line `bookBlob`-scoped `useEffect` from `ebook-reader.tsx` (lines 91–198 in current state on `main`) into a dedicated hook `useEbookReaderInstance()`. **Behavior preserved bit-for-bit.** Pure code reorganization.

## Motivation

The `[bookBlob]`-scoped `useEffect` is the single biggest cluster of imperative glue between React and foliate-js in the reader subsystem. It owns:

- creation and DOM-attachment of the `<foliate-view>` custom element
- wiring the `NavigationController`
- attachment of 5 listener categories (interaction, relocate, load, link/footnote, global resize, global pagehide)
- the `view.open(blob)` flow with initial navigation and char-count startup
- full cleanup including dispose flags

It's structurally one cohesive vertical (the live foliate instance lifecycle), but it's currently inlined in the component, mixed with the rest of `EbookReader`'s state and props. Pulling it into a dedicated hook lets the component become a thin shell composing four hooks (`useFootnoteState`, `useReaderFooter`, `useEbookReaderInstance`, `useImperativeHandle`) plus the small settings-applier `useEffect` and the JSX.

Expected post-distill size of `ebook-reader.tsx`: roughly 90–100 lines (down from current ~217), depending on hook input wiring.

## Scope

### In scope

- New file `frontend/src/hooks/useEbookReaderInstance.ts`.
- New unit tests `frontend/src/hooks/useEbookReaderInstance.test.tsx` (colocated, matching dominant pattern in `frontend/src/hooks/`).
- Refactor `frontend/src/components/ebook-reader.tsx` to consume the hook.

### Out of scope

- The settings-applier `useEffect` (lines 62–81). Stays inline. Separately decided as low-value distill.
- `useImperativeHandle` block (lines 84–88). Stays inline — it owns the public ref shape and reads `viewRef`/`performNavigationRef` directly.
- Any change to `utils/reader-navigation.ts`, `utils/reader-interaction.ts`, `utils/reader-footnote-handler.ts`, `utils/reader-input.ts`, `utils/reader-styling.ts`, `hooks/useReaderFooter.ts`, `hooks/useFootnoteState.ts`, `FootnotePopup.tsx`, foliate-js fork, or any reader-side type.
- Any UX, gesture, navigation, or persistence change.
- `pdf-reader.tsx` (separate epic subtask `qhe`).

## Hook contract

```ts
import type { MutableRefObject, RefObject } from "react";
import type { ReaderSettings } from "../types/reader-settings";
import type { ReaderViewElement } from "../types/reader-foliate";
import type { ReaderNavigationRequest } from "../types/reader-handle";
import type { FootnoteState } from "./useFootnoteState";

export interface EbookReaderInstanceConfig {
  maxInlineSize: string;
  gap: string;
  margin: string | undefined;
  maxBlockSize: string | undefined;
  showFooter: boolean;
  isMobile: boolean;
}

export interface UseEbookReaderInstanceParams {
  bookBlob: Blob;
  initialPosition: string | null | undefined;
  containerRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>;
  viewRef: MutableRefObject<ReaderViewElement | null>;
  performNavigationRef: MutableRefObject<(request: ReaderNavigationRequest) => Promise<void>>;
  callbacksRef: MutableRefObject<{
    onRelocate?: (detail: import("../types/reader-handle").ReaderRelocateDetail) => void;
    onReady?: () => void;
    onSavePosition?: (cfi: string, fraction: number) => void;
  } | undefined>;
  onCenterTapRef: MutableRefObject<(() => void) | undefined>;
  settingsRef: MutableRefObject<ReaderSettings>;
  configRef: MutableRefObject<EbookReaderInstanceConfig>;
  footnote: FootnoteState;
  footer: ReturnType<typeof import("./useReaderFooter").useReaderFooter>;
}

export function useEbookReaderInstance(params: UseEbookReaderInstanceParams): void;
```

Returns nothing. Side-effect-only hook. Internally a single `useEffect` with `[bookBlob]` deps that mirrors today's behavior exactly.

### Why a single big params object

# eqt.1 — `useFootnoteState()` extraction from `ebook-reader.tsx`

**Issue:** librarium-py-eqt.1
**Parent epic:** librarium-py-eqt (F4. Reader subsystem boundary cleanup)
**Date:** 2026-05-05

## Goal

Distill all footnote-related state and refs out of `ebook-reader.tsx` into a single hook `useFootnoteState()`. **Behavior is preserved bit-for-bit.** Pure code reorganization — no UX, no API, no test changes outside of an added unit test for the new hook.

## Motivation

Footnote support in the e-book reader is a coherent vertical: book emits `link` event → handler measures click coordinate → loads section content → opens popup → user dismisses via center-tap. Today this vertical is scattered across `ebook-reader.tsx`:

- 5 React state/refs (`footnoteHtml`, `footnoteSide`, `footnoteOpenRef`, `lastClickXRef`, `lastClickYRef`)
- a dismiss inline closure passed into `attachReaderInteraction`
- prop wiring into `<FootnotePopup>`

Pulling them into a dedicated hook localizes the vertical, reduces the ref count of `ebook-reader.tsx` (from 10 to 7 `useRef` calls), and lets the footnote logic be unit-tested without rendering a `<foliate-view>`.

## Scope

### In scope

- New file `frontend/src/hooks/useFootnoteState.ts`.
- Refactor `frontend/src/components/ebook-reader.tsx` to consume the hook.
- New unit test `frontend/src/hooks/__tests__/useFootnoteState.test.tsx`.
- No changes to `utils/reader-footnote-handler.ts`, `utils/reader-footnotes.ts`, `utils/reader-interaction.ts`, `FootnotePopup`, or any reader-side type.

### Out of scope

- Any change to footnote UX, layout, animation, or content rendering.
- Refactor of other ref clusters in `ebook-reader.tsx` (settings sync, instance init) — covered by future eqt.2/eqt.3.
- `pdf-reader.tsx` (separate epic subtask `qhe`).
- Touching the foliate-js fork.

## Hook contract

```ts
export interface FootnoteState {
  // Reactive UI props for <FootnotePopup>:
  html: string | null;
  side: "left" | "right";

  // Refs handed to imperative integrations:
  isOpenRef: React.MutableRefObject<boolean>;
  clickXRef: React.MutableRefObject<number>;
  clickYRef: React.MutableRefObject<number>;

  // Pre-bundled callbacks for attachFootnoteHandler:
  handlerCallbacks: {
    setFootnoteHtml: (html: string | null) => void;
    setFootnoteSide: (side: "left" | "right") => void;
    setFootnoteOpen: (open: boolean) => void;
    lastClickXRef: { current: number };
  };

  // Dismiss action for attachReaderInteraction's center-tap branch:
  dismiss: () => void;
}

export function useFootnoteState(): FootnoteState;
```

### Internal layout

- `useState` for `html` and `side` (these drive React rerender of `<FootnotePopup>`).
- `useRef` for `isOpenRef`, `clickXRef`, `clickYRef` (read by listeners that live outside React's reconciliation).
- `dismiss = () => { setHtml(null); isOpenRef.current = false; }` — stable identity is **not** required; consumers re-attach `attachReaderInteraction` only when `bookBlob` changes (current useEffect deps).
- `handlerCallbacks` may be reconstructed each render (its consumer, `attachFootnoteHandler`, is itself called inside a `bookBlob`-scoped useEffect and only reads the object once).

### Exported handle

The hook returns one composite object so call sites stay tidy. Consumers destructure the parts they need.

## Behavior preservation

| Existing behavior | How preserved |
|---|---|
| Click coordinate measured per-iframe-doc | `setupFootnoteDocListeners(doc, footnote.clickXRef, footnote.clickYRef)` — same refs, just owned elsewhere. |
| Side computed from `containerWidth / 2` at link-event time | Inside `attachFootnoteHandler` (untouched), reads `lastClickXRef` from `handlerCallbacks`. |
| Center-tap dismisses popup | `attachReaderInteraction(..., { onDismissFootnote: footnote.dismiss, isFootnoteOpen: () => footnote.isOpenRef.current, ... })`. |
| Popup hidden when html is null | `<FootnotePopup html={footnote.html} side={footnote.side} ... />` — same JSX, different source. |
| Open state visible to interaction handler | `isOpenRef` exposed identically; `attachReaderInteraction` reads `.current`. |

## Test plan

### New: `useFootnoteState.test.tsx`

Pin the hook's surface in isolation:

1. **Initial state** — `html === null`, `side === "left"`, `isOpenRef.current === false`, `clickXRef.current === 0`, `clickYRef.current === 0`.
2. **Open via `handlerCallbacks`** — calling `setFootnoteHtml("x")` + `setFootnoteSide("right")` + `setFootnoteOpen(true)` updates `html`, `side`, and `isOpenRef.current` accordingly.
3. **`dismiss()`** — after open, calling `dismiss` clears `html` to `null` and sets `isOpenRef.current` to `false`. `side` is left as-is (current behavior).
4. **Refs are stable across renders** — re-render with no inputs; `isOpenRef`, `clickXRef`, `clickYRef`, `handlerCallbacks.lastClickXRef` keep identity.
5. **Direct ref mutation reflects in interaction view** — writing to `clickXRef.current = 42` is observable to subsequent reads (sanity for the imperative path).

### Existing tests stay green

`reader-footnote-handler.test.tsx`, `reader-footnotes.test.ts`, `reader-interaction.test.tsx`, `useReaderLifecycle.test.tsx`, `ebook-reader.test.tsx` (if exists) — all unchanged, all pass after refactor.

## Manual smoke test (Alexey)

1. Open an EPUB with footnotes; tap a footnote ref → popup appears on correct side based on tap coordinate.
2. Tap center of screen with popup open → popup dismissed, toolbar **not** toggled.
3. Tap center with popup closed → toolbar toggled normally.
4. Open another book → popup state resets.
5. Same checks on FB2 (uses same reader path).

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| `lastClickXRef` shared between document-listener (writes) and footnote-handler (reads) — risk of identity mismatch if hook re-creates ref | Same `useRef` instance returned across renders; `handlerCallbacks.lastClickXRef` references the same object as `clickXRef`. Test #4 pins this. |
| Center-tap dismissal breaks because `isFootnoteOpen` reads stale ref | Hook returns a stable `isOpenRef`; `attachReaderInteraction` already passes `() => isOpenRef.current` (lazy read). |
| Re-rendering the parent recreates `handlerCallbacks` and re-attaches handler | `attachFootnoteHandler` is called inside the `bookBlob`-scoped useEffect; it reads the callbacks once and binds them. New object each render is fine because it isn't passed as a dep. |

# eqt.1 — `useFootnoteState()` extraction from `ebook-reader.tsx`

**Issue:** librarium-py-eqt.1
**Parent epic:** librarium-py-eqt (F4. Reader subsystem boundary cleanup)
**Date:** 2026-05-05

## Goal

Distill all footnote-related state and refs out of `ebook-reader.tsx` into a single hook `useFootnoteState()`. **Behavior is preserved bit-for-bit.** Pure code reorganization — no UX, no API, no test changes outside of an added unit test for the new hook.

## Motivation

Footnote support in the e-book reader is a coherent vertical: book emits `link` event → handler measures click coordinate → loads section content → opens popup → user dismisses via center-tap. Today this vertical is scattered across `ebook-reader.tsx`:

- 5 React state/refs (`footnoteHtml`, `footnoteSide`, `footnoteOpenRef`, `lastClickXRef`, `lastClickYRef`)
- a dismiss inline closure passed into `attachReaderInteraction`
- prop wiring into `<FootnotePopup>`

Pulling them into a dedicated hook localizes the vertical, reduces the ref count of `ebook-reader.tsx` (from 10 to 7 `useRef` calls), and lets the footnote logic be unit-tested without rendering a `<foliate-view>`.

## Scope

### In scope

- New file `frontend/src/hooks/useFootnoteState.ts`.
- Refactor `frontend/src/components/ebook-reader.tsx` to consume the hook.
- New unit test `frontend/src/hooks/__tests__/useFootnoteState.test.tsx`.
- No changes to `utils/reader-footnote-handler.ts`, `utils/reader-footnotes.ts`, `utils/reader-interaction.ts`, `FootnotePopup`, or any reader-side type.

### Out of scope

- Any change to footnote UX, layout, animation, or content rendering.
- Refactor of other ref clusters in `ebook-reader.tsx` (settings sync, instance init) — covered by future eqt.2/eqt.3.
- `pdf-reader.tsx` (separate epic subtask `qhe`).
- Touching the foliate-js fork.

## Hook contract

```ts
export interface FootnoteState {
  // Reactive UI props for <FootnotePopup>:
  html: string | null;
  side: "left" | "right";

  // Refs handed to imperative integrations:
  isOpenRef: React.MutableRefObject<boolean>;
  clickXRef: React.MutableRefObject<number>;
  clickYRef: React.MutableRefObject<number>;

  // Pre-bundled callbacks for attachFootnoteHandler:
  handlerCallbacks: {
    setFootnoteHtml: (html: string | null) => void;
    setFootnoteSide: (side: "left" | "right") => void;
    setFootnoteOpen: (open: boolean) => void;
    lastClickXRef: { current: number };
  };

  // Dismiss action for attachReaderInteraction's center-tap branch:
  dismiss: () => void;
}

export function useFootnoteState(): FootnoteState;
```

### Internal layout

- `useState` for `html` and `side` (these drive React rerender of `<FootnotePopup>`).
- `useRef` for `isOpenRef`, `clickXRef`, `clickYRef` (read by listeners that live outside React's reconciliation).
- `dismiss = () => { setHtml(null); isOpenRef.current = false; }` — stable identity is **not** required; consumers re-attach `attachReaderInteraction` only when `bookBlob` changes (current useEffect deps).
- `handlerCallbacks` may be reconstructed each render (its consumer, `attachFootnoteHandler`, is itself called inside a `bookBlob`-scoped useEffect and only reads the object once).
- **`handlerCallbacks.setFootnoteOpen` is ref-write, not React state.** Implementation: `(open) => { isOpenRef.current = open; }` — mirrors the current inline `ebook-reader.tsx:143`. Do **not** convert to `useState`: `reader-interaction.ts:78` reads via lazy `() => isOpenRef.current` and would receive a stale boolean if open-state were React state.
- **`handlerCallbacks.lastClickXRef` MUST be the same object as the top-level `clickXRef`** (identity equality, not just shape). The inline write in `setupFootnoteDocListeners` (`reader-footnote-handler.ts:69`) and the read in `attachFootnoteHandler` (`reader-footnote-handler.ts:34`) must observe a single shared ref. Test #4 pins this.

### Exported handle

The hook returns one composite object so call sites stay tidy. Consumers destructure the parts they need.

## Behavior preservation

| Existing behavior | How preserved |
|---|---|
| Click coordinate measured per-iframe-doc | `setupFootnoteDocListeners(doc, footnote.clickXRef, footnote.clickYRef)` — same refs, just owned elsewhere. |
| Side computed from `containerWidth / 2` at link-event time | Inside `attachFootnoteHandler` (untouched), reads `lastClickXRef` from `handlerCallbacks`. |
| Center-tap dismisses popup | `attachReaderInteraction(..., { onDismissFootnote: footnote.dismiss, isFootnoteOpen: () => footnote.isOpenRef.current, ... })`. |
| Popup hidden when html is null | `<FootnotePopup html={footnote.html} side={footnote.side} ... />` — same JSX, different source. |
| Open state visible to interaction handler | `isOpenRef` exposed identically; `attachReaderInteraction` reads `.current`. |

## Test plan

### New: `useFootnoteState.test.tsx`

Pin the hook's surface in isolation:

1. **Initial state** — `html === null`, `side === "left"`, `isOpenRef.current === false`, `clickXRef.current === 0`, `clickYRef.current === 0`.
2. **Open via `handlerCallbacks`** — calling `setFootnoteHtml("x")` + `setFootnoteSide("right")` + `setFootnoteOpen(true)` updates `html`, `side`, and `isOpenRef.current` accordingly.
3. **`dismiss()`** — after open, calling `dismiss` clears `html` to `null` and sets `isOpenRef.current` to `false`. `side` is left as-is (current behavior).
4. **Refs are stable across renders** — re-render with no inputs; `isOpenRef`, `clickXRef`, `clickYRef`, `handlerCallbacks.lastClickXRef` keep identity.
5. **`handlerCallbacks.lastClickXRef` is the same object as `clickXRef`** — `expect(result.current.handlerCallbacks.lastClickXRef).toBe(result.current.clickXRef)`. Pins the invariant that the iframe-doc click listener (writes via `clickXRef`) and the link-event handler (reads via `handlerCallbacks.lastClickXRef`) share one ref. A reasonable-looking implementation that builds a separate `{ current: 0 }` proxy in `handlerCallbacks` would silently break click→side coupling and pass test #4.
6. **Direct ref mutation reflects in interaction view** — writing to `clickXRef.current = 42` is observable to subsequent reads (sanity for the imperative path).

### Existing tests stay green

`reader-footnote-handler.test.tsx`, `reader-footnotes.test.ts`, `reader-interaction.test.tsx`, `useReaderLifecycle.test.tsx`, `ebook-reader.test.tsx` (if exists) — all unchanged, all pass after refactor.

## Manual smoke test (Alexey)

1. Open an EPUB with footnotes; tap a footnote ref → popup appears on correct side based on tap coordinate.
2. Tap center of screen with popup open → popup dismissed, toolbar **not** toggled.
3. Tap center with popup closed → toolbar toggled normally.
4. Navigate away from the reader (route change → `EbookReader` unmounts) → reopen book → popup is closed. Note: hook is mount-scoped, not blob-scoped — popup state persists across `bookBlob` changes within a single `EbookReader` mount, same as today.
5. Same checks on FB2 (uses same reader path).

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| `lastClickXRef` shared between document-listener (writes) and footnote-handler (reads) — risk of identity mismatch if hook re-creates ref | Same `useRef` instance returned across renders; `handlerCallbacks.lastClickXRef` references the same object as `clickXRef`. Test #4 pins this. |
| Center-tap dismissal breaks because `isFootnoteOpen` reads stale ref | Hook returns a stable `isOpenRef`; `attachReaderInteraction` already passes `() => isOpenRef.current` (lazy read). |
| Re-rendering the parent recreates `handlerCallbacks` and re-attaches handler | `attachFootnoteHandler` is called inside the `bookBlob`-scoped useEffect; it reads the callbacks once and binds them. New object each render is fine because it isn't passed as a dep. |
| Removing 5 useState/useRef from a component shifts hook order | All 5 are removed together as a unit. The hook call replaces them at the same position. React's "rules of hooks" satisfied. |

## Acceptance

- `ebook-reader.tsx` no longer references `footnoteHtml`/`footnoteSide`/`footnoteOpenRef`/`lastClickXRef`/`lastClickYRef` by those names; it composes `useFootnoteState()`.
- `useRef` call count in `ebook-reader.tsx` drops from 10 → 7. Specifically removed: `lastClickXRef` (line 59), `lastClickYRef` (line 60), `footnoteOpenRef` (line 61).
- `frontend/src/hooks/useFootnoteState.ts` exists with the contract above.
- New test file passes; all existing reader tests pass.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Smoke test items above all pass on Alexey's manual run.

# eqt.1 — Implementation plan: `useFootnoteState()` extraction

**Spec:** `project_documentation/specs/2026-05-05-eqt.1-use-footnote-state-design.md`
**Issue:** librarium-py-eqt.1
**Branch:** `refactor/eqt.1-use-footnote-state` (already created)
**Approach:** TDD per CLAUDE.md — tests before implementation.

## Sequence

### Step 1 — Write failing tests for the hook

**File:** `frontend/src/hooks/__tests__/useFootnoteState.test.tsx` (new).

Six tests, each pinning a distinct invariant from spec §"Test plan":

1. Initial state: `html === null`, `side === "left"`, `isOpenRef.current === false`, `clickXRef.current === 0`, `clickYRef.current === 0`.
2. Open via `handlerCallbacks`: after `setFootnoteHtml("x") + setFootnoteSide("right") + setFootnoteOpen(true)` → `html === "x"`, `side === "right"`, `isOpenRef.current === true`.
3. `dismiss()`: after open, `dismiss()` → `html === null`, `isOpenRef.current === false`. `side` unchanged.
4. Refs stable across renders: re-render → `isOpenRef`, `clickXRef`, `clickYRef`, `handlerCallbacks.lastClickXRef` keep identity (`.toBe(...)`).
5. **Identity invariant:** `expect(result.current.handlerCallbacks.lastClickXRef).toBe(result.current.clickXRef)` — single shared ref.
6. Imperative ref mutation: writing to `clickXRef.current = 42` is observable on next read.

Use `@testing-library/react`'s `renderHook`. No DOM, no `<foliate-view>`, no MSW — pure hook test.

Run: `npm test -- useFootnoteState`. **All six must fail** (file doesn't exist yet) — that's the TDD red.

### Step 2 — Implement the hook

**File:** `frontend/src/hooks/useFootnoteState.ts` (new).

Implement contract from spec §"Hook contract":
- `useState` for `html`, `side`.
- `useRef` for `isOpenRef` (init `false`), `clickXRef` (init `0`), `clickYRef` (init `0`).
- `handlerCallbacks` built each render but containing **the same** `clickXRef` (not a new `{current:0}`).
- `setFootnoteOpen` is ref-write: `(open) => { isOpenRef.current = open; }`.
- `dismiss` is fresh-each-render closure (stability not required).
- Return composite `FootnoteState` object.

Run: `npm test -- useFootnoteState`. **All six pass** — TDD green.

### Step 3 — Wire hook into `ebook-reader.tsx`

In `frontend/src/components/ebook-reader.tsx`:

1. Add `import { useFootnoteState } from "../hooks/useFootnoteState";`.
2. Insert `const footnote = useFootnoteState();` after the existing `useState`/`useRef` calls.
3. Replace consumers:
   - `attachFootnoteHandler(view, container, { setFootnoteHtml, setFootnoteSide, setFootnoteOpen, lastClickXRef })` → `attachFootnoteHandler(view, container, footnote.handlerCallbacks)`.
   - `attachReaderInteraction(..., { ..., isFootnoteOpen: () => footnoteOpenRef.current, onDismissFootnote: () => { setFootnoteHtml(null); footnoteOpenRef.current = false; }, ... })` → `attachReaderInteraction(..., { ..., isFootnoteOpen: () => footnote.isOpenRef.current, onDismissFootnote: footnote.dismiss, ... })`.
   - `setupFootnoteDocListeners(doc, lastClickXRef, lastClickYRef)` → `setupFootnoteDocListeners(doc, footnote.clickXRef, footnote.clickYRef)`.
   - `<FootnotePopup html={footnoteHtml} side={footnoteSide} settings={settings} />` → `<FootnotePopup html={footnote.html} side={footnote.side} settings={settings} />`.
4. Delete the now-unused locals: `footnoteHtml`/`setFootnoteHtml` `useState`, `footnoteSide`/`setFootnoteSide` `useState`, `footnoteOpenRef` `useRef`, `lastClickXRef` `useRef`, `lastClickYRef` `useRef`.

Run: `npm test -- ebook-reader && npx tsc --noEmit`. Both pass.

### Step 4 — Full test suite

`npm test -- --run`. All 720 tests pass (no test outside our two files should change behavior).

### Step 5 — Manual smoke per spec §"Manual smoke test"

Hand off to Alexey. Wait for "ok".

### Step 6 — Commit on branch `refactor/eqt.1-use-footnote-state`

Single commit. Message: `refactor(reader): extract useFootnoteState() hook from ebook-reader (eqt.1)`.

### Step 7 — Spec-vs-code review (CLAUDE.md step 12) + code review (step 13)

Run reviewers, surface ALL findings, fix.

### Step 8 — Merge / push only on Alexey's explicit command (CLAUDE.md steps 15–16).

## Out of plan

- No changes to `utils/reader-footnote-handler.ts`, `utils/reader-interaction.ts`, `utils/reader-footnotes.ts`, `FootnotePopup.tsx`, or any other reader-side file — `attachFootnoteHandler`/`attachReaderInteraction` already accept the shapes we'll feed them.
- No new sibling hooks (`useEbookReaderInstance`, `useReaderSettings` integration) — separate future eqt.X tasks.
- No changes to `pdf-reader.tsx` — separate `qhe`.
- No commits before Step 6.

## Risk register

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Step 3 deletes a line that another consumer in the file still references | Verified: only the listed consumers touch the 5 locals. After Step 3, `tsc --noEmit` will catch any leftover reference. |
| `handlerCallbacks` reconstructed each render → handler re-attached on every render | False risk: `attachFootnoteHandler` is invoked inside the `bookBlob`-scoped `useEffect`, runs once per blob mount. |
| Ref count regression caught only at PR review | Acceptance criterion — explicit grep `grep -c useRef frontend/src/components/ebook-reader.tsx` should report 8 (1 import + 7 calls). Run before commit. |

## Estimated effort

~1.5–2 hours of focused work end-to-end, including manual smoke and reviewer iteration.

Single commit. Message: `refactor(reader): extract useFootnoteState() hook from ebook-reader (eqt.1)`.

### Step 7 — Spec-vs-code review (CLAUDE.md step 12) + code review (step 13)

Run reviewers, surface ALL findings, fix.

### Step 8 — Merge / push only on Alexey's explicit command (CLAUDE.md steps 15–16).

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Step 3 deletes a line that another consumer in the file still references | Verified: only the listed consumers touch the 5 locals. After Step 3, `tsc --noEmit` will catch any leftover reference. |
| `handlerCallbacks` reconstructed each render → handler re-attached on every render | False risk: `attachFootnoteHandler` is invoked inside the `bookBlob`-scoped `useEffect`, runs once per blob mount. |

| `handlerCallbacks` is a fresh object each render — if a future consumer ever places it in a `useEffect` dep array, every render will retrigger that effect | Today's only consumer is `attachFootnoteHandler`, called inside the `bookBlob`-scoped `useEffect` that does NOT list `handlerCallbacks` as a dep — safe. Spec §"Internal layout" already documents this; plan reiterates here so future maintainers see it. |
